title: TECMO WORLD CUP '98 / BLACK CONVERSION
variant: Documented black operator conversion upright with green camouflage deck, two black bat-top sticks and yellow/blue/red actions. Glare-obscured marquee title is adapted from the English Tecmo flyer; no factory-dedicated cabinet or unseen side print is claimed.
preview_note: 32 x 48 | black ST-V conversion / camo deck / 2 bat sticks + 6 actions | flyer title and game screen
hardware: Tecmo 1998 Sega ST-V cartridge / JAMMA operator kit, two-player simultaneous soccer. Hardware corroboration: https://www.arcade-museum.com/Videogame/tecmo-world-cup-98 and https://github.com/mamedev/mame/blob/master/src/mame/sega/stv.cpp (twcup98, ST-V controls). No ROM, core, BIOS or seat configuration changed by this art recipe.

Japanese kit is not silently mixed into the selected English-marquee camo conversion.
operator_art.processing: Original JPEG retained without resizing. Listing page returned HTTP 403; not bypassed. Public museum-linked image used for visual control corroboration only.

uncertainties: ST-V is cartridge/kit hardware; this is a photographed operator conversion, not a claimed unique factory-dedicated Tecmo cabinet. Exact shell maker and region remain unknown.

The accessible front photo shows black edge/inner sides but no full outer side or rear. Those remain plain black with simplified generic service details, not inferred unseen prints. No suitable full side photograph or authenticated operator marquee master was located within bounded research.

The English flyer's title is adapted into the conventional marquee area because the photographed title/instruction band has heavy glare. The photographed lower marquee instructions are not fabricated; neither the promotional soccer player nor Japanese team strip is used as invented side art.

Two bat-top sticks and six yellow/blue/red physical action caps follow the photograph. Two white Start buttons remain in the photographed panel texture. The instruction card's Japanese blue/red/yellow A/B/C diagram differs from the conversion cap order; wiring/action-to-color on the conversion cannot be verified, so physical colors are not claimed as action bindings.

The cabinet screen is powered off. The display texture is actual same-game imagery cropped from the English flyer back, not a fresh local-ROM capture. Flyer printing limits fine detail; aspect is preserved and brightness boosted only at sprite scale.

Shared upright geometry, bat-handle taper and coin/rear service details are pixel-scale approximations rather than factory dimensions. The photograph's three coin windows are simplified by the shared two-slot door.

Both eBay listing pages returned 403; no challenge bypass was attempted. Public image URLs and title association are recorded from the accessible Museum of the Game page. Photos/printed artwork retain underlying rights; permission for redistribution is unresolved.

No twcup98 catalog entry existed when art was started. Integration should select cabinets: ["twcup98"] once its ROM/core configuration is ready. No game configuration is invented, and no map, ROM, upload or deployment is part of this art task.
